title: Defender for Office 365 threat policies switch recipient conditions from AND to OR — and the first edit converts an existing policy
summary: MC1546447 (published 10 November 2026) changes how Defender for Office 365 threat protection policies evaluate recipient inclusion conditions when more than one condition type is set (users, groups, domains): from Match all (AND) to Match any (OR). Rollout to worldwide tenants is planned for early December 2026. New policies use OR by default; existing policies are not converted automatically, but switch to OR the moment an administrator modifies them, in the portal or via Exchange Online PowerShell.
why: Microsoft Learn still documents today's behaviour: different condition types use AND, so 'Users: romain@contoso.com' plus 'Groups: Executives' only hits Romain if he is in Executives. Any policy built on that intersection (strict anti-phishing for a subset of a domain, Safe Attachments dynamic delivery for one business unit at one domain) silently widens on its next routine edit. The portal shows a confirmation; PowerShell only warns when the module is imported, so scripted changes are the risky path.
todo: Inventory rules that combine more than one of SentTo, SentToMemberOf and RecipientDomainIs across Get-AntiPhishRule, Get-SafeLinksRule, Get-SafeAttachmentRule, Get-HostedContentFilterRule and Get-MalwareFilterRule (see the linked recipe).
For each hit, compute the OR population and decide: accept it, or replace the intersection with one dedicated group before anyone edits the policy.
Freeze scripted edits to these rules until December, or add an explicit scope review to the change template.
effective_note: Worldwide rollout planned for early December 2026 (MC1546447). Existing policies change only when modified.
